name: @pipeworx/mcp-ensembl

tools.name: lookup
tools.description: "Ensembl gene info for [ENSG...]" / "look up [Ensembl ID]" / "fetch [ENST.../ENSE.../ENSP...]" — fetch metadata for an Ensembl stable ID (gene / transcript / exon / translation). Returns name, biotype, chromosomal position, strand, description. Pass expand=true to include child features (transcripts of a gene, exons of a transcript). Example: ENSG00000157764 (BRAF).

assembly.description: Human genome build: "GRCh38" (the default) or "GRCh37" (= hg19). Coordinates you pass and coordinates you get back are both in this build. Older variant lists, spreadsheets and published tables are usually GRCh37.

tools.name: lookup_symbol
tools.description: "What's the Ensembl ID for [gene symbol]" / "look up [gene] in Ensembl" / "BRCA1 / TP53 / BRAF Ensembl info" / "find gene [symbol] in [species]" — look up a gene by symbol within a species (e.g. species="human" symbol="BRCA1"). Returns Ensembl gene ID, chromosomal position, biotype, description. Use to convert HGNC gene symbols to Ensembl IDs for genomics workflows.

assembly.description: Human genome build: "GRCh38" (the default) or "GRCh37" (= hg19). Coordinates you pass and coordinates you get back are both in this build. Older variant lists, spreadsheets and published tables are usually GRCh37.

tools.name: xrefs
tools.description: "What's the UniProt / HGNC / RefSeq ID for [gene]" / "cross-references for [gene symbol]" — external database IDs (UniProt, RefSeq, HGNC, Entrez, OMIM, etc.) for a gene symbol. Use to map between bio-database identifier spaces.

tools.name: sequence
tools.description: "DNA / cDNA / CDS / protein sequence of [gene]" / "FASTA for [Ensembl ID]" / "get sequence of [transcript]" — sequence by Ensembl stable ID. Type defaults to "genomic"; pass "cdna", "cds", or "protein" for processed forms. Use for sequence retrieval in primer design, variant analysis, or downstream sequence tools.

assembly.description: Human genome build: "GRCh38" (the default) or "GRCh37" (= hg19). Coordinates you pass and coordinates you get back are both in this build. Older variant lists, spreadsheets and published tables are usually GRCh37.

tools.name: homology
tools.description: "What's the mouse / rat / zebrafish ortholog of [human gene]" / "ortholog of [gene] in [species]" / "homologs of [gene]" — orthologs and paralogs for a gene across species. Use for cross-species comparison, model organism work, evolutionary analysis.

tools.name: variation
tools.description: "What is [rsID]" / "look up SNP [rs...]" / "variant info for [rsN]" — fetch a genetic variation record by ID (e.g. rs56116432). Returns alleles, genomic location, clinical significance, gene mappings. Use for SNP lookups, pharmacogenomics, GWAS follow-up.

assembly.description: Human genome build: "GRCh38" (the default) or "GRCh37" (= hg19). Coordinates you pass and coordinates you get back are both in this build. Older variant lists, spreadsheets and published tables are usually GRCh37.

tools.name: vep
tools.description: "What's the effect of [variant]" / "predict consequences of [genomic change]" / "VEP for [chrom:pos]" — Variant Effect Predictor for a specified region + allele. Returns consequences (missense, synonymous, splice, etc.), affected genes, transcript impacts, SIFT/PolyPhen predictions. Use for variant interpretation in clinical or research genomics. THE REGION IS REQUIRED — there is no default. A GRCh37/hg19 position is also a valid GRCh38 position, so an unstated build cannot be detected, only guessed wrong, and a wrong guess returns confident annotations for a DIFFERENT gene rather than an error.

region.description: e.g. "9:22125504-22125504:1" — in the build named by assembly.

assembly.description: REQUIRED. The genome build your region is in: "GRCh38" (= hg38) or "GRCh37" (= hg19). There is no default on purpose — a genomic position is valid in BOTH builds, so an unstated build cannot be detected, only guessed wrong, and a wrong guess returns confident consequence calls for a different gene instead of an error.

instructions: @pipeworx/mcp-ensembl forwards to the Pipeworx gateway and lists only the ensembl pack's tools. Set PIPEWORX_META_TOOLS=1 to also list ask_pipeworx and the other gateway-wide tools.
